thesis: Chris Dixon argues that the modern Internet has shifted from a decentralized vision where users owned their data and transactions to a consolidated state dominated by a few intermediaries like YouTube and Spotify that capture significant value through high take rates. He posits that while these centralized platforms offer improved user experiences, they threaten creative economies and that blockchain technology serves as a necessary counterbalancing force to prevent further centralization of power and wealth.
